싸우다.forms: 싸워요 · 싸웠어요 · 싸울 거예요 · 싸우지 마세요
싸우다.m: to fight, to argue, to quarrel
싸우다.x: I had a fight with my younger sibling yesterday.
싸우다.e: 싸움 = a fight; 싸우지 마! = Don't fight!

주머니.ex: 저는 휴대폰을 항상 바지 주머니에 넣어요.
주머니.x: I always keep my phone in my pants pocket.
주머니.e: Originally a small cloth pouch tied to traditional clothes, which had no pockets.

무.ex: 무를 넣으면 국 맛이 더 시원해져요.
무.x: Adding radish makes the soup taste more refreshing.
무.e: Homonym warning: the Sino prefix 무- means 'without', as in 무료 'free of charge'.
무.t: For soups, 시원하다 means 'refreshing,' not 'cool' — a classic compliment for radish soup.

없어지다.m: to disappear, to be gone, to be lost
없어지다.x: The wallet I left on the desk is gone.

그림자.x: As evening came, the trees' shadows grew longer.
그림자.e: Probably related to 그리다 'to draw' and 그림 'picture'.

지난번.x: I'll return the book I borrowed last time today.
지난번.t: Usually used with 에 as a time word: 지난번에 'last time'.

전문가.ex: 건강 문제는 전문가와 상담하는 게 좋아요.
전문가.x: For health problems, it's best to consult an expert.
전문가.e: -가 = professional or expert: 전문가, 작가, 화가.

이웃집.ex: 이웃집 아이들이 자주 우리 집에 놀러 와요.
이웃집.x: The neighbor's kids often come over to play.

매표소.ex: 표는 입구 옆에 있는 매표소에서 사세요.
매표소.x: Please buy your ticket at the ticket office next to the entrance.

부딪치다.m: to bump into, to crash into, to collide; to face (a problem)
부딪치다.x: I bumped into someone while looking at my phone on the street.
부딪치다.t: 부딪치다 means actively bumping into something; 부딪히다 means getting hit by something.
rel: to get bumped, to be hit

실망스럽다.x: The movie I had been looking forward to was much more disappointing than I expected.
실망스럽다.e: Literally 'lose hope' plus -스럽다 'seeming, giving that feeling'.
실망스럽다.t: 실망스럽다 describes the thing; for the person, use 실망하다: 저는 실망했어요.

등산복.ex: 주말에 산에 가면 화려한 등산복을 입은 사람이 많아요.
등산복.x: When you go to the mountains on the weekend, lots of people are wearing colorful hiking gear.
등산복.t: Bright, high-tech outdoor wear is famously popular in Korea, and many middle-aged people wear it even off the trail.

전문대.x: I studied nursing at a junior college.

법적.ex: 그 계약은 법적으로 아무 문제가 없어요.
법적.x: That contract has no legal problems at all.
법적.e: -적 turns nouns into '-al' words: 법적, 정치적, 합법적.
법적.t: Pronounced [법쩍]; use 법적 before a noun (법적 문제) and 법적으로 as an adverb.

그리움.x: My longing for my hometown grew bigger and bigger.
그리움.e: Noun from 그립다 (to miss); same root as 그리워하다.

두려움.ex: 실패에 대한 두려움 때문에 시작하지 못했어요.
두려움.x: I couldn't start because of my fear of failure.
두려움.e: Noun form of 두렵다 'to be afraid' (두려우- + -ㅁ).

멍청하다.ex: 열쇠를 집에 두고 오다니 정말 멍청했어요.
멍청하다.x: Leaving my keys at home was really dumb.
멍청하다.t: Blunt and rude toward others; safest when talking about yourself or joking with close friends.

게으름.x: On weekends I want to laze around at home.
게으름.t: Collocation: 게으름을 피우다 means to laze around or slack off.

하물며.m: let alone, much less, all the more
하물며.x: It's hard even for adults, so imagine how it is for a child.
하물며.t: Usually ends in a rhetorical question: 하물며 ~는 어떻겠어요?

다름이 아니라.forms: 다름이 아니라 · 다름이 아니고 (casual) · 다른 게 아니라
다름이 아니라.m: the reason I'm contacting you is…, it's just that…
다름이 아니라.ex: 다름이 아니라 내일 회의 시간을 확인하고 싶어서 연락드렸어요.
다름이 아니라.x: The reason I contacted you is that I wanted to check tomorrow's meeting time.
다름이 아니라.e: Literally 'it is nothing other than': 다르다 'to be different' + 아니다.
다름이 아니라.t: A polite opener for calls, emails and requests, signaling you're getting to the point.

감싸다.m: to wrap, to cover; to protect, to stick up for
감싸다.ex: 엄마는 항상 동생 편을 들고 감싸 줘요.
감싸다.x: Mom always takes my little brother's side and sticks up for him.
감싸다.e: Probably 감다 'to wind' + 싸다 'to wrap': wrapping all the way around.

비키다.m: to step aside, move out of the way
비키다.x: Excuse me, could you please step aside?
비키다.t: A bare 비켜! sounds rude; say 좀 비켜 주세요 or just 잠깐만요.

쨍그랑.x: The glass fell on the floor and broke with a crash.
쨍그랑.e: 의성어 (sound word) for glass or thin metal hitting something hard and ringing or shattering.
쨍그랑.t: Often with 하고 or 소리: 쨍그랑 하는 소리가 났어요. For a big, messy smash, Koreans say 와장창.

비틀거리다.m: to stagger, to totter, to reel
비틀거리다.x: I was so tired that I staggered on the stairs.
비틀거리다.t: Also figurative in the news: 경제가 비틀거리다 'the economy is faltering'.

선거구.x: He ran in his hometown district.

견주다.m: to compare, to measure against; to rival
견주다.ex: 그의 실력은 프로 선수와 견주어도 손색이 없어요.
견주다.x: His skill holds up even when compared with professional athletes.
견주다.e: Picture holding two things side by side to see which measures up; often 견주어 보다.

떠안다.m: to take on (a burden), to be saddled with
떠안다.ex: 회사가 망하면서 그는 큰 빚을 떠안게 됐어요.
떠안다.x: When the company went under, he was saddled with huge debts.
떠안다.e: Built from 떠- 'lift' plus 안다 'to hold in one's arms.'

깔보다.m: to look down on, to belittle
깔보다.ex: 그는 신입 사원들을 깔보는 태도를 보였어요.
깔보다.x: He showed a condescending attitude toward the new employees.
깔보다.e: Memory hook: 깔다 'to spread on the floor' — seeing someone as beneath you.

장병.ex: 대통령이 국군 장병들에게 감사의 뜻을 전했습니다.
장병.x: The president expressed gratitude to the armed forces troops.

약학.x: My older sister is majoring in pharmacy at university.
약학.e: Literally 'medicine studies'. -학 = field of study: 의학, 경제학.
약학.t: Pronounced [야칵]; 약학 is the field of study, while 약국 is the drugstore.

명성.x: That restaurant is widely renowned for its taste.

얼버무리다.m: to evade, give a vague answer, mumble one's way out
얼버무리다.x: When he was asked the question, he gave a vague answer.
얼버무리다.t: Typical objects: 대답을 얼버무리다 or 말을 얼버무리다, 'to dodge with a vague reply.'

집단소송.ex: 피해자 수천 명이 회사를 상대로 집단소송을 준비하고 있어요.
집단소송.x: Thousands of victims are preparing a class action against the company.

파생상품.ex: 파생상품 투자로 큰 손실을 본 사람이 많아요.
파생상품.x: Many people suffered big losses investing in derivatives.
파생상품.e: Literally 'products that branch off' — their value comes from another asset.

금단증상.ex: 담배를 끊으면 처음 며칠 동안 금단증상이 나타나요.
금단증상.x: When you quit smoking, withdrawal symptoms appear for the first few days.

항생물질.x: The first antibiotic substance was discovered by chance in blue mold.
항생물질.e: Literally 'substance against life' — it fights living microbes.
항생물질.t: 항생물질 is the substance itself; the medicine you take is usually called 항생제.

동맥.ex: 동맥은 심장에서 몸 전체로 피를 보내요.
동맥.x: Arteries carry blood from the heart to the whole body.
동맥.e: Literally 'moving vessel' — you can feel it pulse.

심근경색.x: My father was rushed to the emergency room with a heart attack.
심근경색.e: Literally 'heart muscle blocked and stopped up'.
심근경색.t: Everyday speech often says 심장마비 loosely, but 심근경색 is the precise medical term for a heart attack.

고분자.x: Plastic is a typical polymer material.

서술자.ex: 이 소설의 서술자는 주인공의 어린 딸이에요.
서술자.x: The narrator of this novel is the main character's young daughter.
서술자.e: Literally 'one who narrates'; -자 = person: 관찰자, 화자.
서술자.t: Pronounced [서술짜]; for poems, the term is usually 화자 instead.

켜켜이.m: layer upon layer, in thick layers
켜켜이.ex: 책상 위에 먼지가 켜켜이 쌓여 있어요.
켜켜이.x: Dust has piled up in layers on the desk.

백면서생.m: a pale-faced bookworm with no real-world experience
백면서생.ex: 백면서생이라 사회 경험이 부족하다는 말을 들었어요.
백면서생.x: I was told I lack real-world experience, being just a bookworm.
백면서생.e: Literally 'white-faced student' who stays indoors reading.

혈소판.ex: 혈소판 수치가 낮으면 피가 잘 멈추지 않아요.
혈소판.x: If your platelet count is low, bleeding doesn't stop easily.
혈소판.e: Literally 'blood small plates', just like English 'platelet'.
